items.summary: In this unpublished per curiam opinion filed November 13, 2026, the Eighth Circuit affirmed a within-Guidelines sentence imposed on Medard Elonge after he pleaded guilty to conspiring to defraud the United States. The court granted counsel's Anders motion to withdraw, held that the guilty plea was knowing and voluntary, and found no abuse of discretion in the district court's implicit denial of a motion to withdraw the plea. items.summary: On November 13, 2026, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit issued an opinion in No. 25-1460, Alton Antrim v. Jared Hoy, affirming the district court's judgment for the Wisconsin Secretary of Corrections. The court held that Wisconsin's lifetime GPS monitoring requirement under WIS. STAT. § 301.48, as applied to individuals with two or more sex-offense convictions, is reasonable under the Fourth Amendment, applying its prior decisions in Braam v. Carr and Belleau v. Wall. The excerpt also describes the monitoring device, the exclusion-zone review process, the petition procedures for ending monitoring, and a class of approximately 740 people certified in the district court.
items.title: Alton Antrim v. Jared Hoy

items.summary: In Rogers v. Social Security Administration, the Sixth Circuit affirmed the district court's judgment upholding the Social Security Administration's denial of supplemental security income benefits to Heather Rogers. The court held that the ALJ's residual functional capacity finding for light work was supported by substantial evidence, including the ALJ's decision to find the opinion of examining physician Dr. Samuel Kimmell unpersuasive and to discount Rogers's statements about her symptoms. The opinion was issued by a panel consisting of Judges Cole, Sutton, and Thapar.

items.summary: In United States v. Jerry W. Dunn, the Sixth Circuit affirmed Dunn's convictions on five counts of sexual exploitation of a minor under 18 U.S.C. § 2251(a) and one count of possession of child sexual abuse material under 18 U.S.C. § 2252(a)(4)(B), along with his 720-month sentence. The court held that Dunn's challenges to witness testimony and chain of custody raised questions of credibility and weight rather than sufficiency of the evidence. It also held that the below-Guidelines sentence was substantively reasonable under the presumption of reasonableness, and the opinion is not recommended for publication.

William Lee, et al., the Sixth Circuit reversed the district court's judgment on the Tennessee sex offender registration classification claim, holding that the classifications operate retrospectively but do not impose punishment and that TBI Director David Rausch is a proper defendant for that claim. Michigan State Police, et al., the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit affirmed the district court's dismissal of a complaint by individuals registered under Michigan's Sex Offender Registration Act (SORA), who alleged that SORA's in-person reporting requirements effect seizures under the Fourth Amendment. items.summary: In an opinion recommended for publication and filed November 13, 2026, the Sixth Circuit, in consolidated appeals Nos. 25-1413/1414 (Doe v. Whitmer), affirmed in part, vacated in part, and remanded a decision of the Eastern District of Michigan concerning Michigan's Sex Offenders Registration Act as amended in 2021. The opinion describes the district court's findings that the retroactive application of the 2021 amendments violates the Ex Post Facto Clause and that the Michigan State Police's treatment of individuals with non-Michigan convictions violates procedural due process, as well as its rejection of other constitutional challenges. The opinion also recounts the statute's history, including its 1994 enactment, its move to a public registry, and its 2011 amendments responding to the federal Sex Offender Registration and Notification Act.

items.summary: In this unpublished per curiam opinion, the Eleventh Circuit affirmed the conviction of Jelani Petersen for attempting to entice a minor to engage in unlawful sexual activity under 18 U.S.C. § 2422(b). The court held that the district court did not err in granting the government's motion in limine and refusing an entrapment instruction, because the defendant did not produce evidence of government inducement beyond an opportunity to commit the offense. The court also stated that the text messages supported the district court's conclusion that the defendant intended to avoid police detection rather than abandon his intent to commit the offense.
items.title: USA v. Jelani Petersen

items.summary: Reported by Senator Lee from the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources with an amendment on November 12, 2026, S. 1254 amends subsection (c) of the Aquifer Recharge Flexibility Act. It allows a holder, or a State, political subdivision, Indian Tribe, or public entity acting for the holder, to use an existing right-of-way, easement, permit, or other authorization for aquifer recharge without additional authorization from the Secretary, provided notice is given to the Bureau of Land Management at least 30 days in advance. The use is exempt from additional rent to the Bureau of Land Management, except for for-profit uses or for-profit entities; the reported text contains two overlapping versions of the effect provision, which differ on whether compliance with the Federal Water Pollution Control Act, the Endangered Species Act of 1973, and the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act is waived.
items.title: 119 S1254 RS: To amend the Aquifer Recharge Flexibility Act to clarify a provision relating to conveyances for aquifer recharge purposes.

items.summary: Reported by Senator Lee from the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources with an amendment on November 12, 2026, S. 2262, the American Voices in Federal Lands Act, amends the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976. It defines citizen of the United States in section 103 to include certain natural persons born in or naturalized in the United States and certain juridical persons domiciled in the United States, and it provides that the citizenship of a legal representative cannot cure ineligibility. The bill limits the Secretary of the Interior, when promulgating regulations for Bureau of Land Management lands, to considering public comments from citizens of the United States and requires a process using the best available technology to deter public involvement by others, while stating that public comments submitted by mail are not affected.
items.title: 119 S2262 RS: American Voices in Federal Lands Act

items.opening_verbatim: II Calendar No. 706 119th CONGRESS 2d Session S. 4116 IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES March 17, 2026 Mr. Hickenlooper (for himself, Mr. Daines , Mr. Padilla , and Mr. Curtis ) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and refer
items.summary: Reported by Senator Lee from the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources with an amendment on November 12, 2026, S. 4116, the Geothermal Power Opportunity With Expanded Regions Act or Geo POWER Act, amends section 615 of the Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007. It establishes a Milestone-Based Geothermal Demonstration Program, to be set up by the Secretary of Energy within 180 days, that awards innovative financing through a competitive process to geothermal projects in low-permeability and impermeable reservoirs, prioritizing projects in regions with limited geothermal generation, including on or near Indian land. The bill requires awards to not fewer than three proposals in at least three States and to not fewer than three project sponsors, and authorizes $800,000,000 to remain available until expended, of which up to $750,000,000 is for the demonstration projects and up to $50,000,000 is for program administration.
items.title: 119 S4116 RS: Geothermal Power Opportunity With Expanded Regions Act

items.opening_verbatim: II Calendar No. 708 119th CONGRESS 2d Session S. 4846 IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES June 22, 2026 Mr. Kelly (for himself and Mr. Cornyn ) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and N
items.summary: Reported by Senator Lee from the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources without amendment on November 12, 2026, S. 4846, the Transboundary Aquifer Assessment Program Act or TAAP Act, amends the United States-Mexico Transboundary Aquifer Assessment Act. It adds Arizona to the States in which priority transboundary aquifers may be designated, excluding an aquifer underlying Arizona and Sonora, Mexico, that is partially within the Yuma groundwater basin designated by a 1984 order of the Arizona Department of Water Resources. The bill replaces the authorization of appropriations for fiscal years 2007 through 2016 with authorization for fiscal years 2026 through 2036 and updates the sunset provision to refer to the Transboundary Aquifer Assessment Program Act.
items.title: 109 S4846 RS: Transboundary Aquifer Assessment Program Act

items.summary: Reported by Senator Lee from the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources with an amendment on November 12, 2026, S. 789, the Critical Minerals Security Act of 2025, requires the Secretary of the Interior, in consultation with other federal agencies, to submit to Congress a report within one year of enactment and every two years thereafter on critical mineral and rare earth element resources worldwide. The reports assess control of those resources by foreign entities of concern and by the United States or allied countries, and cover mine outputs, beneficial ownership, and cases of forced divestment or government takeover of mining and processing operations. The bill also requires the Secretary to establish a process for United States persons seeking to divest foreign critical mineral operations and to develop, with allied governments, a strategy for advanced mining, processing, and recycling technologies, with annual progress reports to Congress.
items.title: 119 S789 RS: Critical Minerals Security Act of 2025
